title: Noah Uncovered
notes: This chunk delivers a tight double reading of Genesis 8:13 that locks the flood log to the sixth seal while keeping the plain sense primary. Strengths include the clean assembly of echad/ot/shanah into seals of the age, consistent lexicon work, and the firm close that never unseats the ship's log. Residual presenter staging is heavy (Mark three things, Do what this part, Now read, Hold this, Now weigh, sit down and try). Multiple author-prose sentences open with And or But, one fingerprint clause is tangled, and 'make Noah the righteous' is awkward. Surgical replacements restore assertive density without touching doctrine or quoted text.

proposals.old: Mark three things before moving on.
proposals.summary: Remove director cue at paragraph open.
proposals.rationale: House style forbids Mark that / Mark three staging; the assertion of the three marks keeps the author's density and voice.

proposals.old: And Jesus took this narrative, of all narratives, as the type of the end: __“as it was in the days of Noe, so shall it be also in the days of the Son of man”__ (Luke 17:26).
proposals.new: Jesus took this narrative, of all narratives, as the type of the end: __“as it was in the days of Noe, so shall it be also in the days of the Son of man”__ (Luke 17:26).
proposals.rationale: Author prose must not begin with And; the claim and scripture citation remain identical.

proposals.old:
Do what this part of the book has learned to do.
Remove the vowel points, and ask what else the letters say.
proposals.new: Remove the vowel points, and ask what else the letters say.
proposals.summary: Cut pure meta-instruction before the method.
proposals.rationale: Do what this part has learned is presenter staging; the following imperative already carries the book's established method.

proposals.old: And the waters have been defined since this book's fourth chapter: __“the sym:sym-sea[waters]… are *peoples*, and multitudes, and nations”__ (Revelation 17:15).
proposals.new: The waters have been defined since this book's fourth chapter: __“the sym:sym-sea[waters]… are *peoples*, and multitudes, and nations”__ (Revelation 17:15).
proposals.rationale: Author prose must not begin with And; the definition and citation stay intact.

proposals.old: The verb __“removed”__ is singular; make Noah the righteous — a company — and the singular verb goes looking for a singular subject: *God took up* the righteous, __“caught up together… to meet the Lord”__ (1 Thessalonians 4:17).
proposals.new: The verb __“removed”__ is singular; read Noah as the righteous — a company — and the singular verb goes looking for a singular subject: *God took up* the righteous, __“caught up together… to meet the Lord”__ (1 Thessalonians 4:17).
proposals.summary: Replace awkward 'make Noah' with method language.
proposals.rationale: Make Noah the righteous is unclear and slightly director-like; read Noah as matches the letter-reading practice used throughout the chapter.

proposals.old: Now read the whole verse the second time through:
proposals.new: The whole verse a second time through:
proposals.summary: Remove Now-read director cue before the re-reading.
proposals.rationale: House style forbids Now read / Read that staging; the colon still introduces the second reading cleanly.

proposals.old: Hold this reading to the same law as every reading in this book.
proposals.new: This reading holds to the same law as every reading in this book.
proposals.rationale: Hold that / Hold this is forbidden director language; the rewritten sentence keeps the identical legal claim in the author's voice.

proposals.old:
Now weigh what this verse would cost to write.
A poet can rhyme a line; a careful author can plant a pun and land it.
But sit down and try to compose twelve consecutive words that read as a dated entry in a ship's log — grammar sound, narrative plain — while the same letters, pointed differently, read as the sixth seal of a book that would not be written for two and a half millennia: every alternate sense attested, every symbol matching the definitions Scripture gives elsewhere, the two readings never fouling each other from the first word to the last.
proposals.new:
What this verse would cost to write stands clear.
A poet can rhyme a line; a careful author can plant a pun and land it.
Composing twelve consecutive words that read as a dated entry in a ship's log — grammar sound, narrative plain — while the same letters, pointed differently, read as the sixth seal of a book that would not be written for two and a half millennia: every alternate sense attested, every symbol matching the definitions Scripture gives elsewhere, the two readings never fouling each other from the first word to the last, exceeds ordinary craft.
proposals.summary: Remove Now-weigh and But-sit-down staging while preserving the cost claim.
proposals.rationale: Now weigh and sit down and try are explicit director cues; the rewrite asserts the same impossibility of the double reading without meta-instruction or forbidden sentence opens.
